project: Auto Body Repair Chain Expansion Analysis
decomposition_rationale: Sizing engagement decomposed along three branches: (1) Market demand estimation per metro, (2) Competitive landscape analysis, (3) Logistics and location optimization. Custom categories used for auto-body-specific analyses that do not map to standard enum. DAG structure reflects that location optimization depends on both demand and competition data.

tasks.description: Estimate annual auto body repair demand across top 50 US metro areas using vehicle population, accident rates, weather patterns, and average repair spend
acceptance_criteria: Demand estimate for each of top 50 metros with explicit methodology
At least 3 data sources for demand drivers (vehicle registration, NHTSA accident data, weather/road condition data)
Sensitivity analysis on accident rate assumptions
Demand segmented by repair type (collision, paintless dent, cosmetic)
tasks.anti_confirmatory_framing: Evaluate demand for auto body repair services including evidence for both growing demand (aging vehicle fleet, rising repair costs) and declining demand (improved vehicle safety, autonomous driving reducing accidents, insurance policy changes)
tasks.end_product: Metro-level demand table (50 rows x demand metrics), demand heat map, sensitivity analysis on 3 key drivers

tasks.description: Map competitive density of auto body repair shops per metro area: shops-per-capita, revenue-per-shop, chain vs independent mix, recent entry/exit trends
acceptance_criteria: Competitive density metric for each of top 50 metros
Chain vs independent breakdown where data available
Identification of under-served and over-served markets
Correlation analysis between density and market profitability indicators
tasks.anti_confirmatory_framing: Evaluate competitive dynamics including evidence that high-density markets may still be attractive (due to market growth or inefficient incumbents) and that low-density markets may have structural barriers to entry (insufficient demand, regulatory hurdles)
tasks.end_product: Competitive density table (50 metros), density vs profitability scatter plot, under-served market identification matrix

tasks.description: Analyze insurance industry dynamics affecting auto body repair demand: DRP (Direct Repair Program) penetration, insurer concentration by metro, and impact on independent shop economics
acceptance_criteria: DRP penetration rates for top 10 insurers by metro area where available
Assessment of DRP impact on repair shop margins and volumes
Trends in insurer consolidation affecting repair shop negotiations
Implications for new market entrant economics
tasks.anti_confirmatory_framing: Evaluate insurance industry dynamics including evidence both for DRP programs being beneficial to chain operators (guaranteed volume) and detrimental (margin compression, loss of pricing power)
tasks.end_product: DRP penetration summary by metro tier, insurer concentration heat map, margin impact analysis

tasks.description: Map existing distribution hub locations and model logistics costs (parts shipping, technician travel, equipment sharing) as a function of distance from hubs to candidate expansion metros
acceptance_criteria: Distance matrix between existing 12 metro hubs and candidate expansion metros
Logistics cost model with explicit assumptions
Identification of optimal hub-and-spoke clusters
Sensitivity to shipping cost assumptions
tasks.anti_confirmatory_framing: Evaluate the logistics optimization model including evidence both for hub proximity being a decisive factor (significant cost savings) and for hub proximity being secondary to demand and competition factors
tasks.end_product: Hub-to-metro distance matrix, logistics cost curves, optimal cluster map, hub expansion recommendations

tasks.description: Assess commercial real estate costs and availability for auto body repair facilities across candidate metro areas
acceptance_criteria: Average industrial/commercial lease rates for candidate metros
Zoning and environmental requirements for auto body shops
Real estate availability assessment (vacancy rates for suitable properties)
Build-out cost estimates for standard facility format
tasks.anti_confirmatory_framing: Evaluate real estate factors including evidence for both favorable conditions (high vacancy, low lease rates) and unfavorable conditions (zoning restrictions, environmental remediation costs, gentrification pressures) in candidate markets
tasks.end_product: Real estate cost comparison table (50 metros), zoning feasibility scorecard, site type availability matrix

tasks.description: Build composite location scoring model integrating demand, competition, logistics, and real estate factors. Produce ranked list of top 50 metros with recommended first tranche of 8 locations.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-factor scoring model with explicit weights and methodology
Ranked list of all 50 metros by composite score
Recommended first tranche of 8 locations with supporting rationale
Sensitivity analysis showing how ranking changes under different weight profiles
tasks.anti_confirmatory_framing: Evaluate the location ranking model including stress tests that challenge the weighting assumptions and evidence for alternative prioritization frameworks that would produce materially different rankings
tasks.end_product: Composite scored metro ranking table (50 rows), recommended first tranche with risk-adjusted rationale, sensitivity spider chart showing weight impact
